head: Tapko Octaver guitar octave app turns your guitar into bass on iPhone
dek: Tapko Octaver shifts a guitar signal one octave down into bass range, for single-note bass lines and riffs, for $2.99 on iPhone and iPad. It came out on 23 November and was #41 among paid Music apps on the US App Store that day.
details: Controls set the bass and sub levels, pick attack, tone, saturation, compression and the mix between guitar and octave, with a low-latency mode. A second pitch voice goes from one octave down to one octave up for fifths and harmonies, and there's a three-band EQ, a noise gate and four starter presets. It runs on its own with headphones and an audio interface or the built-in mic, or as an Audio Unit plugin in apps such as GarageBand, AUM, Loopy Pro and Cubasis. It's made by David Lars Guva and needs iOS 17 or later.
where: iPhone and iPad (iOS 17 or later), App Store, $2.99
means: If you play guitar and want bass lines without a bass or a pedal, this app does it on a phone or tablet you already have.
todo: Use headphones or an audio interface for the cleanest sound, and try it inside GarageBand if you record there.
